# n_n01

# Interview: You're asked to explain a caching system design. What happens if you've always relied on AI to design systems?
If I have always relied on AI to design systems, I may struggle to explain a caching system design during an interview. I may not know what data to cache, where to store it, or how to handle cache expiration, and consistency. This could make it hard to justify my design choices or answer follow-up questions.

# n_02.

# Production Bug: At 2 AM, you must debug code generated by AI months ago - but AI is offline. Can you fix it?
if I need to debug code generated by AI months ago but AI is offline, I may find it very hard to fix issues quickly. Without understanding the code and its logic, I would have to spend extra time tracing through it.

# n_03.

# New Technology: A new library is released, and AI hasn't been trained on it yet. How do you learn it?
When a new library is released and AI hasn’t been trained on it, I must rely on my own learning skills. I would read the documentation, and sufficient practices with examples for better underestanding.


# Reflection: Write one paragraph explaining how using AI fairly today prepares you for real-world challenges like these..  

Using AI fairly means using AI a as learning tool to aid/enhance our learning process/understanding rather than a shortcut that bypasses effort. When I use AI as a learning supprort to clarify concepts, explain logic, or provide structured guidance, I remain  actively engaged in problem-solving skill process. This strengthen my analytical reasoning, reinforece my conceptual mastery and build my intellectual independence.
